subject: Workplace Skills
title: Writing for Clarity
description: Learn Writing for Clarity in one minute.

hook.text: A remote team lost a week because a Slack message said 'handle the API issue' without specifying which one.

buildup.text: In-person, you can ask 'which one?' instantly. Remote, that question costs hours due to timezone gaps.

discovery.text: Include context, specifics, and expected action in every message. Treat each one like a mini-brief.

twist.text: Over-communicating feels redundant to the writer but saves everyone else from guessing and waiting.

climax.text: Before sending, ask: if someone reads this in a different timezone with no context, will they know what to do?

punchline.text: Say what, why, and what's needed. Every time.

quiz.question: What's the key principle of writing for remote teams?
options: Keep messages as short as possible
Include enough context that someone in another timezone can act
